name: P9 — Direction-specific rubric
description: P9: completeness and scientific quality under the accompanying task specification. Integrity is evaluated in the separate integrity rubric.

deliverables.title: Deliverable presence (Tier 1 gates)
deliverables.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Does proposal/report.pdf exist with substantive content (full sections, not a placeholder)?
leaves.evidence: Filesystem check: stat proposal/report.pdf; verify Methodology / Experimental Setup / Results / Analysis / Conclusion sections.

yes.description: report.pdf exists and contains a substantive paper.
yes.criteria: PDF exists, parses cleanly, and contains the required sections with non-placeholder content.

no.criteria: PDF absent, malformed, or contains only placeholder text.

leaves.question: Does proposal/logs/ exist with non-empty per-run records?
leaves.evidence: Filesystem check: ls proposal/logs/; spot-check files for actual emulator output.

yes.description: logs directory present with run records.
yes.criteria: proposal/logs/ exists with files documenting baseline emulations, variant emulations, and kernel-derivation outputs.

no.criteria: Directory absent, empty, or contains only placeholder files.

leaves.question: Does proposal/code/kernel_plan.{py,md,json} exist with the chosen axis (1/2/3), the kernel's mathematical form, and the validation sweep grid stated up front?
leaves.evidence: proposal/code/kernel_plan.* file; check the timestamp predates the validation run timestamps.

yes.criteria: File exists, names the chosen axis, declares the kernel's mathematical form (xi(k) as a function), the kernel-family being claimed, the test problem choice, and the validation sweep grid; modification time predates the earliest validation log entry.

no.criteria: File absent, doesn't declare the axis/kernel/sweep grid, or modification time is after validation runs began.

leaves.question: Are kernel-derivation artifacts (scaling derivation, admissibility verification, discretized weights, QSVT-angle generation) present at proposal/code/kernel_derivation/?
leaves.evidence: proposal/code/kernel_derivation/ contents — analytical derivation or citation, admissibility check, discretized weight construction script, QSVT angle generator with intermediate validation.

yes.criteria: Directory contains scripts or notebooks that (a) derive or cite the kernel's scaling, (b) verify An-Childs-Lin admissibility (or approximate-LCHS conditions), (c) construct the discretized weights w_j, (d) generate QSVT angles for the kernel-encoded weight function with polynomial-approximation validation.

no.criteria: Directory empty, contains only stubs, or kernel is asserted in the paper without reproducible derivation.

leaves.question: Are Novikau-Joseph beta-family baseline emulations logged at the headline configuration (n_x=6, n_k=6) and at the validation sweep configurations?
leaves.evidence: proposal/logs/baseline/ contents — circuit-construction inputs, QSP angles, emulator outputs, gate-count tallies, success-probability traces.

yes.criteria: Logs exist for the Novikau-Joseph beta-family circuit at the headline configuration and at the sweep configurations the variant is compared against; all metrics (gate counts, ancilla counts, Q_A, accuracy, success probability) recorded.

no.criteria: At least one baseline configuration is missing from the logs.

leaves.question: Are variant (kernel-substituted) emulations logged at the same configurations as the baseline?
leaves.evidence: proposal/logs/variant/ contents — same configurations as baseline, same logging structure.

yes.criteria: Every configuration the baseline was run on has a corresponding variant emulation with all metrics logged.

no.criteria: At least one configuration is missing from the variant logs.

leaves.question: Are kernel-family characterization sweep runs logged at >=3 (n_k, eps_LCHS) combinations (for all axes), or >=4 eps_LCHS targets at headline (n_x, n_k) for axis 1?
leaves.evidence: proposal/logs/sweep/ contents — characterization runs spanning the declared grid.

yes.criteria: Logs cover the declared sweep grid for the kernel-family characterization (>=3 (n_k, eps_LCHS) combinations); for axis 1, also the precision-scaling sweep at >=4 eps_LCHS targets.

no.criteria: Declared sweep grid not fully covered by logged runs.

leaves.question: Is the main results table present (tab:main_results) with columns for method, test, (n_x, n_k, t, eps), final relative error, STMC gate count, Q_A, ancillae, success prob.? (Gate complexity is reported as STMC gate count; CNOT/T/Toffoli are out of scope for this task since QuCF compiles to the STMC gate set.)
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex; locate tab:main_results.

yes.criteria: Table includes baseline and variant rows for the headline and characterization sweep configurations, with all columns filled from logged data.

no.description: Main results table missing or incomplete.
no.criteria: Table absent, missing rows or columns, or has placeholder cells.

leaves.question: Is the axis-specific scaling/reduction figure present (Q_A vs log(1/eps) for axis 1; ancilla-count table or plot for axis 2; gate-count vs ||At|| or 1/eps plot for axis 3)?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex figures matching the chosen axis.

yes.criteria: Figure exists with baseline and variant overlaid, fitted exponents (axis 1) or per-configuration reductions (axis 2/3) explicit.

no.criteria: Required axis-specific figure absent.

leaves.question: Is the kernel-family characterization figure/plot present (which family is best at which (n_k, eps_LCHS) regime)?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex; locate the kernel-family characterization figure or table.

yes.criteria: Figure or table shows the kernel-family-vs-resolution comparison across the declared sweep grid.

no.criteria: No figure or table characterizes which family is best at which resolution.

leaves.question: Does proposal/codebase_notes.md document what was inspected in code/QuCF/, code/QuCF-OPT-LCHS/, and the wiki?
leaves.evidence: Filesystem check + content inspection.

yes.criteria: Notes identify which QuCF / QuCF-OPT-LCHS components were reused for the selector circuit, FCC quadrature driver, QSVT weight construction; state which were reused, which were patched, which were extended.

no.criteria: File absent, empty, or contains only placeholder text.

leaves.question: Is proposal/attempts_log.md present and substantive when partial / unresolved work is claimed?
leaves.evidence: Filesystem check + content inspection; cross-reference with paper claims of partial work.

yes.description: Attempts log substantive (or unused but present).
yes.criteria: File exists and either documents distinct approaches with stated rationale, or the paper claims no partial work.

no.description: Attempts log missing when partial work is claimed.
no.criteria: Paper claims partial/failed/unresolved work but attempts_log.md is absent or trivial.

leaves.question: Does the paper contain a Methodology section stating the kernel and derivation outline before any results?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex section structure.

yes.criteria: Section explicitly states the kernel's mathematical form, hyperparameters, theoretical scaling, and admissibility before any empirical results.

no.criteria: No Methodology section, or kernel is first introduced after results.

kernel_specification.title: Kernel specification and axis commitment
kernel_specification.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Does the paper commit to exactly one of the three axes (1: Q_A, 2: ancillae, 3: gates) with the axis stated in Methodology before any results?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex Methodology section; cross-check with proposal/code/kernel_plan.

yes.criteria: Paper names the chosen axis explicitly in Methodology; same axis appears in kernel_plan.

no.description: Axis not committed or multiple axes mixed.
no.criteria: Paper attempts multiple axes without commitment, or axis is implicit / changes between Methodology and Results.

leaves.question: Which numeric axis did the submission commit to as its headline: Axis 1 (query complexity Q_A), Axis 2 (quantum memory / ancilla count), or Axis 3 (gate complexity)?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex Methodology + proposal/code/kernel_plan (the committed axis).

axis_1.criteria: Headline axis is Axis 1 (Q_A query complexity in precision).

axis_2.criteria: Headline axis is Axis 2 (ancilla count). The below-baseline success-probability exception applies only here.

axis_3.criteria: Headline axis is Axis 3 (STMC gate count).

leaves.question: Is the kernel xi(k) stated as a precise mathematical function with all parameters explicit?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex Methodology — the kernel's mathematical statement.

fully_specified.criteria: xi(k) is a closed-form function with all parameters (beta, k_max, contour parameters, polynomial degree if relevant) explicit; reimplementable from the paper alone.

mostly_specified.criteria: Kernel stated as a function but at least one parameter is left as a TBD or one component is implicit.

qualitative_only.criteria: Kernel described in prose without a precise mathematical statement.

leaves.question: Is the kernel's theoretical scaling on the chosen axis derived in the paper or cited from a published result?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex Methodology — the scaling argument or citation.

derived.criteria: Paper provides a derivation (full or sketch) of the chosen kernel's asymptotic scaling on the chosen axis, traceable from the kernel's form.

cited.criteria: Scaling is asserted with a specific citation to a published derivation; citation is verifiable.

asserted_without_basis.criteria: Scaling is claimed without derivation or specific citation.

leaves.question: Does the kernel satisfy the An-Childs-Lin admissibility conditions (decay, normalization, continuity, lower-half-plane analyticity) for exact LCHS, OR the documented approximate-LCHS conditions if an approximate kernel is used?
leaves.evidence: proposal/code/kernel_derivation/ admissibility check + proposal/report.tex statement.

verified.criteria: Each of the four An-Childs-Lin conditions (or approximate-LCHS analogues) is explicitly verified, either analytically with proof or with a documented numerical check.

mostly_verified.criteria: Most conditions verified but at least one is asserted without explicit check.

not_verified.criteria: Admissibility is asserted in prose without specific verification of the named conditions.

leaves.question: Was the QSVT weight construction genuinely reworked for the substituted kernel — new QSVT angles computed and verified to reproduce the new weight function, a weight-selection option added to the LCHS code, and the full LCHS run verified end to end with the new weights?
leaves.evidence: proposal/code/kernel_derivation/ angle-finding + verification; weight-selection option in the LCHS code; proposal/logs/ standalone-weight and end-to-end LCHS verification.

reworked_and_verified.criteria: New QSVT angles are computed and verified to reproduce the new weight function within a stated tolerance, the weight-selection option is added, and the full LCHS algorithm is verified end to end with the new weights.

reworked_unverified.criteria: The weights are reworked for the new kernel but at least one verification step (angle precision, standalone-weight check, or end-to-end LCHS check) is missing or incomplete.

not_reworked.criteria: The weight construction is not genuinely reworked for the new kernel (e.g., the hard-coded baseline weights are reused), so the kernel substitution is not actually realized in the circuit.

implementation_framework_preserved.title: Novikau-Joseph implementation framework preserved
implementation_framework_preserved.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Does the variant use FCC-equivalent quadrature via the sinusoidal coordinate transformation k = k_max sin(theta) as in the original paper, not a substituted quadrature?
leaves.evidence: proposal/code/ quadrature implementation; cross-check against the paper's framework.

yes.criteria: The variant maps the integration variable via k = k_max sin(theta) with the Chebyshev-extrema discretization; FCC-equivalence is preserved.

no.criteria: Variant uses a different quadrature scheme (e.g., composite Gaussian, Simpson, an analytic-extension-specific quadrature) without justification or disclosure.

leaves.question: Does the variant use a single QSP circuit selector (not a sequence of N_k controlled time-evolution operators, not a multiplexed block-encoding)?
leaves.evidence: proposal/code/ selector implementation.

yes.criteria: Variant maps the discretized LCHS sum to a single QSP circuit of qubitization operators, as in the Novikau-Joseph framework.

no.criteria: Variant uses Ref. [24]'s multiplexed block-encoding, a sequence of controlled time-evolutions, or other selector design.

leaves.question: Does the variant use QSVT for weight construction (U_sqrt(w) operator) as in the original paper, with the QSVT polynomial adapted to the new kernel?
leaves.evidence: proposal/code/ weight-construction implementation.

yes.criteria: Variant keeps the QSVT weight-construction interface (U_sqrt(w) + amplitude amplification) and reworks the QSVT polynomial/angles for the new kernel's weight function.

no.criteria: Variant abandons the QSVT weight-construction interface entirely (e.g., direct state preparation, a different unitary synthesis) without justification.

leaves.question: Are the block-encoding costs of A_L and A_H counted within all reported gate / query / ancilla metrics?
leaves.evidence: proposal/code/ gate-counting pipeline + proposal/logs/ recorded metrics.

yes.criteria: Every gate / query / ancilla metric includes the cost of the A_L and A_H block-encodings (state preparation, controlled-SWAP, arithmetic subroutines as applicable).

no.criteria: Block-encoding costs are excluded by treating A_L, A_H as oracles without constructing them, inflating the apparent improvement.

baseline_verification.title: Novikau-Joseph baseline verification
baseline_verification.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Does the baseline reproduction at the headline configuration (n_x=6, n_k=6) achieve end-to-end relative error consistent with the paper's reported behavior (epsilon_LCHS in 10^-3 to 10^-4 at n_k=6 with beta in [0.7, 0.8])?
leaves.evidence: proposal/logs/baseline/headline/ final relative error.

yes.criteria: Reproduced baseline's relative error at the headline configuration is within an order of magnitude of the paper's reported epsilon_LCHS at the same beta.

no.criteria: Reproduced baseline diverges qualitatively from the paper's reported behavior.

leaves.question: Does the baseline reproduction's success probability at the headline configuration match the paper's reported ~0.2?
leaves.evidence: proposal/logs/baseline/headline/ success probability.

yes.criteria: Reproduced success probability is within ~30% of 0.2 (a reasonable emulator-to-paper variance).

no.criteria: Reproduced success probability is far from 0.2, indicating a misconfigured baseline.

scaling_improvement.title: Scaling improvement on the chosen axis
scaling_improvement.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: On the chosen axis, does the variant achieve strictly better scaling than the Novikau-Joseph baseline per the axis's operationalization?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex Results — axis-specific scaling/reduction analysis; cross-check with proposal/logs/.

strictly_better.criteria: Axis 1: fitted scaling exponent statistically lower than baseline across >=4 eps targets, AND headline Q_A below baseline at matched accuracy, AND consistent with kernel's theoretical scaling. Axis 2: ancillae strictly less than baseline at >=3 configurations including headline at eps<=10^-3, AND success probability not collapsed. Axis 3: STMC gate count strictly less than baseline at >=3 configurations including headline at eps<=10^-3, AND empirical scaling exponent no worse than baseline.

marginal_or_inconclusive.criteria: Variant shows some improvement at some configurations but does not meet the strict criterion (fewer than 3 winning configurations, fit not statistically significant, headline not improved, scaling exponent worse than baseline on axis 3, or success probability collapsed on axis 2).

no_improvement.criteria: Variant does not improve over baseline on the chosen axis.

regression.criteria: Variant is strictly worse than baseline on the chosen axis at the headline or at multiple sweep points.

leaves.question: Is the improvement on the chosen axis confirmed at the headline configuration (n_x=6, n_k=6) at the announced eps_LCHS target?
leaves.evidence: proposal/logs/variant/headline/ vs proposal/logs/baseline/headline/.

yes.criteria: At the headline configuration, the variant's chosen-axis metric (Q_A, ancillae, or gates) is strictly less than the baseline's at matched accuracy.

no.criteria: Variant matches or worsens the baseline at the headline.

leaves.question: Does the empirically measured scaling agree with the kernel's stated theoretical scaling within a factor of 2-3 across the sweep?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex Results — empirical vs theoretical scaling comparison.

agrees_well.criteria: Fitted scaling exponent (axis 1) or per-configuration reduction (axis 2/3) is consistent with the theoretical scaling within a factor of 2-3.

agrees_loosely.criteria: Empirical scaling shows the predicted trend but with a 3-10x prefactor gap; paper discusses why.

disagrees.criteria: Empirical scaling does not show the predicted asymptotic trend, or shows a different exponent than the kernel's theoretical scaling.

leaves.question: Is the variant's end-to-end relative state-vector error no worse than the baseline's at the same (n_x, n_k, t, eps_LCHS) target?
leaves.evidence: proposal/logs/variant/ vs proposal/logs/baseline/ across all sweep configurations.

yes.criteria: At every sweep configuration, the variant's relative state-vector error is at or below the baseline's at the same precision target.

no.criteria: At at least one configuration, the variant's relative error exceeds the baseline's.

leaves.question: How does the variant's success probability compare to the baseline's ~0.2 across all sweep configurations (including any required amplitude-amplification rounds counted in the gate metric)? On Axis 2, a success probability below baseline is acceptable if the paper proves it does not get worse with problem size.
leaves.evidence: proposal/logs/variant/ success probability + AA cost; scale-stability argument in the paper.

preserved.criteria: Variant's success probability is at or above baseline's at every sweep configuration; if AA is used to recover probability, the AA cost is included in the gate metric.

below_but_scale_stable_proven.description: Below baseline but proven scale-stable (Axis 2 exception).
below_but_scale_stable_proven.criteria: Variant's success probability is below baseline's on one or more configurations, but the paper proves it does not get worse with problem size, and any AA cost used to recover probability is counted in the gate metric. Assignable ONLY when the committed axis (kernel_specification.axis_number) is Axis 2; on Axis 1 or Axis 3 a below-baseline success probability must be scored 'collapsed'.

collapsed.criteria: Variant's success probability is below the baseline's with no scale-stability proof, or the additional AA cost is not disclosed in the metric.

kernel_family_characterization.title: Kernel-family characterization across (n_k, eps_LCHS) regimes
kernel_family_characterization.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Is the characterization sweep run completely at the declared (n_k, eps_LCHS) combinations (>=3 for all axes; >=4 eps targets for axis 1 in addition)?
leaves.evidence: proposal/logs/sweep/ coverage vs proposal/code/kernel_plan.

yes.criteria: Every sweep point in kernel_plan has corresponding logged emulator output for both baseline and variant.

no.criteria: At least one declared sweep point is missing from the logs.

leaves.question: Does the characterization identify the regime boundaries (crossover points where a different family wins) between baseline and variant?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex characterization figure + analysis.

boundaries_clear.criteria: Paper identifies specific (n_k, eps_LCHS) regimes where each kernel family wins, with reasoning tied to the kernels' analytical structure.

boundaries_partial.criteria: Paper notes regime differences but does not identify the boundaries precisely.

no_boundary_analysis.criteria: Paper reports per-configuration results without engaging with how the kernel-family winner varies across the sweep.

leaves.question: Is a substantive kernel-family characterization figure/table present, covering which family performs best at each declared n_k/error-target regime? Assess coverage and interpretability here; falsified figure data are an integrity question.
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex characterization figure vs proposal/logs/sweep/.

yes.description: The figure/table covers the declared sweep grid and distinguishes its regimes.

no.description: The figure/table is absent, omits declared regimes, or does not support the required characterization.

mechanism_analysis.title: Mechanism analysis
mechanism_analysis.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Does the paper contain an explicit mechanism subsection in the Analysis section?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex Analysis section.

yes.criteria: Analysis section has an explicit subsection on mechanism.

no.criteria: Paper reports kernel and results without explaining the mechanism.

leaves.question: How deeply does the mechanism analysis explain the kernel's behavior within the implementation framework?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex Analysis section content.

deep.criteria: Analysis connects the kernel's analytical structure (decay rate, contour behavior, polynomial-degree dependence) to the empirically observed scaling on the chosen axis; explains why the FCC quadrature + QSP-selector combination is well-matched to this kernel.

moderate.criteria: Analysis identifies the key kernel features that produce the scaling but does not trace to the implementation framework in detail.

shallow.criteria: Analysis restates the kernel and results without explaining the mechanism.

leaves.question: Does the paper give a clear explanation of why the chosen kernel is the optimal choice in practice at the emulated resolutions (why it wins over the other characterized kernel families in this framework), not only its asymptotic scaling?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex Analysis / mechanism + kernel-family characterization.

yes.criteria: The paper explains, with reference to the characterization data, why the chosen kernel is best in practice at the emulated resolutions.

no.criteria: The kernel choice is asserted or justified only asymptotically, without explaining why it wins in practice.

failure_analysis.title: Failure analysis
failure_analysis.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Does the paper contain an explicit failure-analysis subsection?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex Analysis section.

yes.criteria: Analysis section explicitly discusses where the variant does not improve.

no.criteria: Paper does not discuss limits of the variant's improvement.

leaves.question: Are specific failure patterns identified (e.g., 'the variant loses to baseline at low n_k because the kernel's discretization error dominates' or 'the variant's improvement shrinks at high accuracy targets because the QSVT polynomial degree saturates')?
leaves.evidence: Failure subsection content.

yes.criteria: Patterns are stated concretely (which parameter regime, which configuration, with mechanistic reasoning).

no.criteria: Failure modes mentioned generically without identifying the specific regime.

leaves.question: Are the failure patterns explained coherently, tied to the kernel's analytical structure or the implementation framework's constraints?
leaves.evidence: Failure subsection content.

yes.criteria: Each pattern is connected to a specific feature of the kernel or implementation.

no.criteria: Patterns identified but explanations are post-hoc or hand-wavy.

compute_cost_analysis.title: Computational cost analysis (classical-side)
compute_cost_analysis.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Does the paper contain an explicit computational-cost subsection?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex Analysis or Methodology section.

yes.criteria: Explicit subsection discusses classical-side costs.

no.criteria: Paper does not discuss classical-side cost.

leaves.question: Is the classical-side cost of the variant (QSVT angle generation, kernel weight construction, polynomial-approximation construction) quantified relative to the baseline?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex cost discussion + proposal/logs/timing/.

yes.criteria: Concrete wall-clock or operation-count measurements for the variant's classical-side cost vs the baseline's, with the ratio explicit.

no.criteria: Cost discussed qualitatively without numbers.

originality_and_literature.title: Originality and literature engagement
originality_and_literature.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Is the kernel original relative to published kernels in the LCHS / approximate-LCHS / analytic-extension literature (Refs. [24, 25, 33] of the paper and follow-ups)? Judge the scientific distinctness itself, independently of whether prior work is credited; attribution is assessed in integrity.
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex Related Work + Methodology positioning.

tiers.name: distinct_contribution
tiers.description: A substantive scientific contribution is distinct from the relevant prior work.

tiers.name: meaningful_extension
tiers.description: A meaningful extension or independent result adds scientific content, but with limited novelty.

tiers.name: substantive_replication
tiers.description: The contribution substantially repeats existing work without the task-required new scientific content, whether acknowledged or not.

tiers.name: not_established
tiers.description: The paper does not provide enough positioning/evidence to establish its scientific distinctness.

leaves.question: How substantively does the paper engage with the relevant published literature (LCHS, approximate-LCHS, analytic-extension, Koopman-von Neumann quantum algorithms)?
leaves.evidence: Related Work section + in-text citations.

substantial.criteria: Paper cites and discusses 8+ relevant references across LCHS variants, approximate-LCHS, analytic-extension, KvN; explicit comparison of contributions.

moderate.criteria: Paper cites several references but does not deeply discuss the comparison.

shallow.criteria: Few citations beyond the original Novikau-Joseph paper; no meaningful comparison with optimal-kernel literature.

leaves.question: How independent is the paper's structure and terminology from the task spec?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex structure; section titles; terminology.

fully_independent.criteria: Paper reads as a self-contained journal contribution; no use of phrases like 'axis 1', 'kernel-substitution direction', 'Novikau-Joseph baseline' verbatim.

partially_independent.criteria: Paper structure mostly journal-style but uses some spec terminology.

transliterated.criteria: Paper section structure and terminology mirror the task spec.

writing_quality.title: Writing quality
writing_quality.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Does the paper read as a journal-quality contribution in structure and prose?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex overall structure and prose.

journal_quality.criteria: Clear thesis, claims supported by quantitative evidence, prose-driven main sections, careful citations.

reasonable.criteria: Structure and prose are clear but lack polish.

poor.criteria: Disorganized structure, prose absent, or claims regularly unsupported.

leaves.question: Is an explicit, substantive limitations discussion present and adequate for evaluating the work's scientific scope? Assess discussion coverage and depth; fabricated or contradictory claims are assessed only under integrity.
leaves.evidence: Limitations or Conclusion subsection.

tiers.name: substantive
tiers.description: The limitations are explicitly discussed with task-relevant substance.

tiers.name: perfunctory
tiers.description: A discussion is present but superficial.

leaves.question: Is the rendered PDF free of formatting issues (overflowing equations, broken figures, cut-off tables)?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.pdf visual inspection.

yes.criteria: No equation overflow, no broken cross-references, all figures and tables render correctly.

no.criteria: Equations overflow, references broken, figures cut off, tables overflow.

leaves.question: Is the main results table complete with all rows and columns filled from logged data?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex tab:main_results.

yes.criteria: All baseline and variant rows + characterization sweep rows present; all metric columns filled from logs.

no.criteria: Missing rows or cells with placeholders.

assessment_policy.scope: Completeness and scientific quality only: required artifacts, executed experimental coverage, reproducible methodology, mathematical/statistical validity, performance targets, and task-required analysis/writing.
assessment_policy.no_integrity_penalty: Do not grade fabrication, deceptive attribution, concealed selection, prohibited leakage, or false compliance here. Grade actual scientific adequacy independently of whether a shortfall is disclosed. Integrity evidence is assessed only in integrity_check_rubric.json.
assessment_policy.authoritative_task: The accompanying unchanged task specification controls required versus optional work and permitted exceptions. A qualitative quality tier is not authority to introduce a new experiment, resource limit, or numerical minimum absent from the task.
assessment_policy.conditional_nodes: Respect applicability. Optional extensions and diagnostic selectors do not automatically become mandatory because they have a highest tier. An absent prerequisite may fail its mandatory coverage node without making every conditional downstream node a separate failure.
assessment_policy.inference: Insufficient scientific support is not itself dishonesty. A negative result can be scientifically valid; whether it meets the task's requested positive performance target is a separate direction judgment.
